summary: Search engines ignore URL fragments after #, so subheadings link to the page top (local TOCs help, or make separate pages for critical content), and the first ~140 characters serve as the search description.
questions: Why do search results link to the top of the page instead of the section?
What text do search engines show as the description of a docs page?

answer_card.title: Other search hints
answer_card.answer_md:
- Search engines ignore `#` fragments, so results point to the page top. Local TOCs help; critical topics may deserve their own page.
- Without description metadata, search engines show the **first ~140 characters**, so make the opening sentences describe the page clearly.
